warnings.warning: Eq.3 combines a volumetric conduction term with h(T_ext-T) while h is printed in surface-convection units; no interface factor or volumetric reinterpretation is supplied.
Eq.4 is a first-normal-derivative flux boundary, but the prose calls it a third-order PDE.
Eq.5 uses q0 whose Table 2 unit is printed W/(s m), inconsistent with an ordinary heat-flux density.
Eq.7 uses two-rack area 2S, while the capacity-only Eq.11 uses S before Eq.12 restores the factor of two.
Eq.8 uses sigma_i without fully reconciling Table 3 variance, standard-deviation, and per-unit columns; tests use 0.3861 and 0.2048.
Eq.9 grouping is typographically compact and is fully clarified only by the expanded Eq.21.
Eq.13 W/L notation and Fig.9 L/W orientation are not reconciled.
Eq.17 lacks derivation and stable l/S_l notation; the visual transcription is retained at medium confidence.
Eq.20 uses Z+ without defining whether zero counts are allowed, although absent shapes require zero.
Eq.20 retains four shape families, but the source alternates between m>=12 and m>10 for the circle approximation, leaving m=11 unresolved.
The source omits transient initial data, dimensional closure, mesh, tolerance, and numerical convergence for Eq.1-Eq.5.
Eq.27-Eq.31 verify arithmetic for three scenarios but do not establish search completeness, holdout validity, or robustness.

visualization_dispositions.analytical_purpose: Open-top pan geometry defines bottom, sides, and boundary facets for the physical model.
Heat-flow arrows distinguish pan conduction and oven convection before the PDE.
Finite-element square temperature surface with kelvin colorbar shows corner concentration.
Square edge-temperature curve shows corner highs and edge-center lows against position.
Circle temperature surface supplies the near-uniform limiting comparison.
Aligned edge curves compare square through 16-gon under fixed area and parameters.
Numerical overall and edge dispersion statistics provide the optimization lookup.
Sigma versus inverse squared edge count visualizes the Eq.6 fit.
Packing sketches explain nominal area utilization and unused spaces.
Rack and rectangle dimensions expose the Eq.13 containment variables.
Rectangle arrangement illustrates the p=1 maximum-count branch.
Triangular and square circle-center lattices compare p=0 arrangements.
Rectangle, octagon, and hexagon diagrams show edge and interior waste mechanisms.
Dodecagon-to-circle comparison motivates the circle approximation for large m.
Heptagon and other polygon diagrams document excluded packing families.
Octagon edges and center matrix turn close packing into a point representation.
Hexagon diagram exposes the source's special boundary and rotation conditions.
Flowchart records input, matrix construction, containment tests, counting loop, and output.
Commercial oven, racks, and pan images establish scenario provenance but not validation data.
Two candidate arrangements for each retained shape define the search catalogue.
Test 1 hexagon layout visualizes N=40 for p=0.5 and W/L=9/13.
Test 2 octagon layout visualizes N=30 for p=0.25.
Test 3 octagon layout visualizes the neighboring aspect-ratio decision change.
Sharp-versus-rounded corner geometry and fields communicate a prospective improvement mechanism.
